title: Build pipeline upgrade master page
content: Goal: every build job runs on the new runner pool with a shared cache, and the median build finishes in under 12 minutes. Status: 62 of 80 build jobs now run on the new runner pool. The median build time is down from 18 to 11 minutes. The shared cache serves 81% of build steps, up from 64%. Key issues: PLAT-1, PLAT-4, PLAT-5 and PLAT-6. PLAT-1 is blocked because it waits on finance approval for the host order. Plan of record: the Runner pool rollout plan in Drive. Decided: jobs move in groups of ten, and each group runs a full night before the next one moves. Owner: Ruben Schmidt.

title: Runner pool design
content: This design explains how the two racks and the runner labels serve every build job. 62 of 80 build jobs run on the new pool and 18 still use the old one. Jobs move in groups of ten, and each group runs a full night before the next one moves. Runner labels decide which jobs each rack accepts. Designed by Lina Engel and reviewed by Ines Brandt. Open question: Can the iOS jobs move before the second rack is in place?

title: Build cache design
content: This design explains how the shared build cache is filled, keyed and cleared. The shared cache serves 81% of build steps, up from 64% before the upgrade. The cache warm-up takes 11 minutes and runs before the nightly builds. Only builds on the main branch write to the shared cache. Designed by Lina Engel and reviewed by Ada Pereira. Open question: Can the cache warm-up run before the nightly builds?

title: Decision record: one shared cache for every branch
content: Context: fork builds may read from the shared cache but never write to it. Decision: one shared cache serves every branch, and only the main branch writes to it. Cache keys include the lockfile hash, so a dependency bump starts a fresh entry. Chiara Walsh approved this after the review.

title: Decision record: automatic quarantine for flaky tests
content: Background: the flaky test rate dropped from 3.1% to 0.9% of runs. Decision: a test is quarantined after three failures in a row on the main branch. Every quarantined test gets an owner within one working day. Approved by Rosa Dubois at the team sync.

title: Decision record: batching in the merge queue
content: Context: the merge queue will test up to 6 pull requests in one batch. Decision: the merge queue batches up to six pull requests, and urgent fixes run alone. The average wait in the merge queue is 9 minutes. Amara Juarez approved this after the review.

title: Playbook: runner queue backlog
content: Use this playbook when jobs wait more than 5 minutes for a runner. Step 1: Check the queue time panel on the build dashboard. Step 2: Pause new job moves if any job waits more than 5 minutes for a runner. Step 3: Add hosts from the spare pool before moving the next group. Escalate to Ines Brandt if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Playbook: cache hit rate drop
content: Use this playbook when a job's cache hit rate falls below 50%. Step 1: Find the job on the cache panel of the build dashboard. Step 2: Compare its hit rate with the week before. Step 3: Clear the job's cache entry if its hit rate drops below 50%. Escalate to Ruben Schmidt if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Playbook: full runner disk
content: Use this playbook when a build fails because a runner disk is full. Step 1: Check which runner reports a full disk. Step 2: Run the cleanup job on that runner. Step 3: Take the runner out of the pool if its disk fills again within a day. Escalate to Lukas Larsen if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Pipeline sync: rack capacity
content: Attendees: Amara Juarez, Ada Pereira and Chiara Walsh. Discussed: the first rack carries 32 runners and the second rack will add 24 more. Risk raised: the host order could slip by two weeks if finance approval waits for the budget review. Decided: jobs move in groups of ten, and each group runs a full night before the next one moves. Follow-up: PLAT-14 removes the autoscaler that served the old pool.

title: Pipeline sync: merge queue batching
content: Attendees: Ada Pereira, Lina Engel and Lukas Larsen. Update: an urgent label lets a fix skip the batch and run alone. Risk raised: large batches could hide which pull request broke the build. Decided: the merge queue batches up to six pull requests, and urgent fixes run alone. Action: PLAT-28 limits each branch to 4 parallel jobs.

title: Pipeline sync: flaky test review
content: Attendees: Lina Engel, Lukas Larsen and Amara Juarez. Discussed: the team that owns a folder owns its quarantined tests. Risk raised: quarantine could hide a real fault if nobody reads the list each week. Decided: a test is quarantined after three failures in a row on the main branch. Next step: PLAT-22 lists flaky tests by failure count and owner.

title: How to move a job to the new runner pool
content: This guide explains how to move a build job to the new runner pool. First, check the queue time panel on the build dashboard. Then pause new job moves if any job waits more than 5 minutes for a runner. Finally, add hosts from the spare pool before moving the next group. Ask in #plat-runners if something fails.

title: How to read the build dashboard
content: This guide explains how to read the build dashboard. First, open the build dashboard and pick a job. Then check its queue time, cache hit rate and duration. Finally, open the slowest stage to see where the time goes. Ask in #plat-dashboard if something fails.

title: How to release a test from quarantine
content: This guide explains how to release a test from quarantine. First, open the flaky test dashboard and sort by failures this week. Then fix the test or agree a date with its owner. Finally, release the test from quarantine after ten green runs. Ask in #plat-flaky-tests if something fails.

title: Runner labels and pools
content: This page covers the runner labels, racks and pools. The 18 remaining jobs are the iOS and Android packaging jobs. Each runner on the new pool has 16 cores and 64 GB of memory. The old pool runs on 70 hosts that are three years past their support date.

title: Build time budget
content: This page describes how the pull request pipeline stays under 12 minutes. The backend test suite runs in 8 shards balanced by recorded duration. No shard runs longer than 6 minutes on the new pool. The 40 slowest integration tests are moving into their own nightly job. Rosa Dubois owns this design, and Lina Engel reviewed it.

title: Retrospective: the first 40 jobs
content: Attendees: Chiara Walsh, Lina Engel and Dmitri Ueda. Discussed: the new runner pool has 56 hosts across two racks. Risk raised: the host order could slip by two weeks if finance approval waits for the budget review. Decided: jobs move in groups of ten, and each group runs a full night before the next one moves. Action: PLAT-4 moves the 9 Android packaging jobs to the new runner pool.

title: Mobile app 4.0 release master page
content: Goal: version 4.0 reaches every customer through a staged rollout, with a crash-free rate of at least 99.5%. Status: the 4.0 release candidate passed store review on Android and waits on review for iOS. The staged rollout sits at 10% of Android users. The crash-free rate on the beta is 99.6%, up from 99.2%. Key issues: MOB-1, MOB-3, MOB-13 and MOB-18. MOB-3 is blocked because it waits on the store review team to reply. Plan of record: the Mobile 4.0 rollout plan in Drive. Decided: the release train leaves every second Thursday, with hotfixes in between only for crashes. Owner: Theo Lund.

title: Release train design
content: This design explains how builds move from the main branch to the stores every second Thursday. Hotfixes go out between trains only when the crash-free rate drops below 99%. The release candidate carries 212 merged pull requests. Only crash fixes merge after the branch freeze on Tuesday. Ingrid Tanaka owns this design, and Esther Fischer reviewed it. Open question: Can the offline mode fix still make the 4.0 train?

title: Decision record: staged rollout steps
content: Background: release captains raise each step from the store console. Decision: each rollout step waits 48 hours and needs a crash-free rate of 99.5%. The iOS rollout starts at 5% once store review passes. Gustav Eriksen approved this after the review.

title: Decision record: offline sync conflicts
content: Background: offline mode keeps the last 30 days of activity on the phone. Decision: the most recent edit wins a sync conflict. Photos taken offline upload only on Wi-Fi. Tomas Castillo approved this after the review.

title: Playbook: crash spike during rollout
content: Use this playbook when crashes double within an hour during a rollout step. Step 1: Pause the rollout from the store console. Step 2: Check the top crash on the crash dashboard. Step 3: Ship a hotfix on the next train or roll back to the previous build. Escalate to Tomas Castillo if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Playbook: store review rejection
content: Use this playbook when a store reviewer rejects a build. Step 1: Read the reviewer's message in the store console. Step 2: Fix the build or answer the question within one working day. Step 3: Resubmit the build and note the new review time in the release channel. Call Dario Dias if it is not fixed within an hour.

title: Mobile sync: rollout at 10%
content: Attendees: Dario Dias, Tomas Castillo and Ingrid Tanaka. Update: the rollout reaches every Android user about ten days after the first step. Risk raised: the iOS rollout could slip if store review asks for another change. Decided: each rollout step waits 48 hours and needs a crash-free rate of 99.5%. Action: MOB-13 starts the iOS rollout at 5% once store review passes.

title: Mobile sync: beta feedback review
content: Attendees: Gustav Eriksen, Esther Fischer and Theo Lund. Discussed: the beta needs 300 testers with phones older than four years. Beta feedback is triaged every Monday. Follow-up: MOB-27 closes the 4.0 beta once the rollout passes 50%.

title: Mobile sync: store review status
content: Attendees: Ingrid Tanaka, Andre Hoffmann and Tomas Castillo. Discussed: the location privacy label changes in 4.0. The Android build passed review on the first try. Follow-up: MOB-16 updates the privacy label for the new location prompt.

title: How to cut a release branch
content: This guide explains how to cut a release branch for the train. First, check that the beta sign-off is recorded for the build. Then cut the release branch from the main branch at the agreed commit. Finally, post the branch name and the freeze time in the release channel. Ask in #mob-release if something fails.

title: How to run a staged rollout
content: This guide explains how to raise a staged rollout to its next step. First, check the crash-free rate for the current step. Then raise the rollout to the next step in the store console. Finally, post the new percentage in the release channel. Ask in #mob-release if something fails.

title: Accessibility checklist for new screens
content: This page covers what every new screen needs before it ships. Every button on the new home screen has a screen reader label. The accessibility audit found 9 problems and 7 are fixed. The two open audit findings are on the settings screens.

title: New home screen design
content: This design explains the layout and colours of the new home screen. Usability tests with 12 customers found the new layout faster. Dark theme colours were adjusted to meet the contrast guideline. The new home screen ships on both platforms in 4.0. Designed by Andre Hoffmann and reviewed by Theo Lund. Open question: Will the new home screen colours change before the release?

title: Offline mode design
content: This design explains how the app stores activity and syncs changes offline. Sync conflicts resolve in favour of the most recent edit. Offline mode is behind a flag for 20% of beta testers. The next build shows when the app last synced and what is waiting to upload. Theo Lund owns this design, and Dario Dias reviewed it.

title: Performance budget for 4.0
content: This page describes the startup, size and scrolling limits for 4.0. Cold start time dropped from 2.8 to 1.9 seconds. The app grew by 4 MB because of the new fonts. Three startup tasks no longer block the first screen. Esther Fischer owns this design, and Tomas Castillo reviewed it.

title: Retrospective: the 4.0 beta
content: Attendees: Dario Dias, Rafael Costa and Tomas Castillo. Update: the beta has 1,840 testers across both platforms. The beta sign-off needs two weeks without a new top crash. Next step: MOB-19 recruits 300 beta testers with phones older than four years.

title: Customer data warehouse master page
content: Goal: every product team reads customer metrics from one warehouse, with data no older than two hours. Status: 21 of 30 ingestion jobs now load into the new warehouse. 26 of 30 main tables meet the two-hour freshness target. 14 of 20 product dashboards read from the new warehouse. Key issues: DATA-1, DATA-2, DATA-6 and DATA-21. DATA-2 is blocked because it waits on read access to the billing source. Plan of record: the Warehouse rollout plan in Drive. Decided: every ingestion job writes to a staging table before the main table. Owner: Bjorn Owusu.

title: Warehouse architecture
content: This design explains how staging tables, main tables and dashboards fit together. The customer table holds one row per account with 42 columns. Main tables are partitioned by day and clustered by account. 26 of 30 main tables meet the two-hour freshness target. Designed by Pavel Abara and reviewed by Celine Kowalski.

title: Decision record: staging before main tables
content: Background: 21 of 30 ingestion jobs load into the new warehouse. Decision: every ingestion job writes to a staging table before the main table. The event stream job loads 48 million rows a day. Pavel Abara approved this after the review.

title: Decision record: quality checks stop dashboards
content: Background: nightly row counts are compared with each source system. Decision: a failed quality check stops the linked dashboards from refreshing. Null checks caught three broken loads in the last four weeks. Approved by Zara Garcia at the team sync.

title: Playbook: failed nightly load
content: Use this playbook when a nightly load fails after its three retries. Step 1: Find the failed job on the ingestion dashboard. Step 2: Read the error from the last retry. Step 3: Rerun the job from its staging table once the source is back. Call Celine Kowalski if it is not fixed within an hour.

title: Playbook: stale dashboard
content: Use this playbook when a dashboard shows data older than two hours. Step 1: Open the freshness view and find the stale table. Step 2: Check whether its ingestion job failed or ran late. Step 3: Post the expected refresh time in the dashboards channel. Escalate to Celine Kowalski if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Data sync: dashboard moves
content: Attendees: Pavel Abara, Leon Torres and Celine Kowalski. Discussed: 14 of 20 product dashboards read from the new warehouse. The churn dashboard refreshes every hour. Next step: DATA-19 moves the activation dashboard to the new warehouse.

title: Data sync: backfill planning
content: Attendees: Zara Garcia, Bjorn Owusu and Leon Torres. Discussed: the support tickets backfill covers three years of history. Risk raised: a long backfill could overlap working hours and slow the dashboards. Decided: backfills run only between 22:00 and 06:00. Follow-up: DATA-27 backfills three years of support tickets.

title: How to add a quality check
content: This guide explains how to add a quality check to a main table. First, write the check as a query that returns the failing rows. Then add it to the check catalogue with an owner. Finally, run it against last night's load before you merge it. Ask in #data-quality if something fails.

title: How to request a large query
content: This guide explains how to request approval for a query that scans more than 50 GB. First, estimate the scan size with a dry run. Then ask the table owner for approval in the costs channel. Finally, run the query outside working hours if it scans more than 200 GB. Ask in #data-costs if something fails.

title: Column naming guide
content: This page explains how warehouse columns are named and described. Main tables are partitioned by day and clustered by account. New column names follow the naming guide. 26 of 30 main tables meet the two-hour freshness target.

title: Schema change process
content: This page explains how a schema change is reviewed and announced. A breaking change is announced two weeks before it applies. New columns are added at the end of a table. Renamed columns keep an alias for two weeks.

title: Freshness targets
content: This design explains the two-hour freshness target and how it is measured. Freshness is measured as the age of the newest row. The support tickets table runs about three hours behind on a typical day. Freshness is checked every 15 minutes. Designed by Clara Rahman and reviewed by Pavel Abara.

title: Customer churn model review
content: This design explains the churn model features the risk team reviews. The churn model scores every account each night. Churn model inputs come from the customer and activity tables. Risk analysts review the model features once a month. Designed by Pavel Abara and reviewed by Zara Garcia. Open question: Who signs off the churn model features?

title: Retrospective: the event backfill
content: Attendees: Clara Rahman, Zara Garcia and Celine Kowalski. Update: the two-year backfill of events finished in six nights. Risk raised: a long backfill could overlap working hours and slow the dashboards. Decided: backfills run only between 22:00 and 06:00. Action: DATA-27 backfills three years of support tickets.

title: KYC review automation master page
content: Goal: analysts clear the review queue within one working day, with every decision backed by audit evidence. Status: the review queue holds 340 cases, down from 1,200. Automatic checks clear 58% of cases without an analyst. The median handling time is 14 minutes, down from 31. Key issues: KYC-1, KYC-2, KYC-6 and KYC-18. KYC-18 is blocked because it waits on the risk committee's next meeting. Plan of record: the Automation rollout plan in Drive. Decided: cases are picked in order of risk score, not arrival time. Owner: Yara Nowak.

title: Review queue design
content: This page describes how cases enter, wait in and leave the review queue. Cases older than one working day are flagged in red. Analysts pick cases in order of risk score. The queue is staffed from 08:00 to 20:00 on weekdays. Arjun Weber owns this design, and Maren Strand reviewed it. Open question: Can we stop weekend cover once automation clears half the queue?

title: Decision record: queue order by risk score
content: Background: the review queue holds 340 cases, down from 1,200. Decision: cases are picked in order of risk score, not arrival time. The queue is staffed from 08:00 to 20:00 on weekdays. Approved by Pavel Abara at the team sync.

title: Decision record: replay before tuning
content: Background: name matching ignores accents and word order. Decision: every tuning change is replayed on past alerts before it goes live. False positives fell from 71% to 44% of alerts. Approved by Yara Nowak at the team sync.

title: Playbook: queue backlog over 500
content: Use this playbook when the review queue grows past 500 cases. Step 1: Move two analysts from alert tuning to the queue. Step 2: Pause sample reviews until the queue drops under 400 cases. Step 3: Post the queue size in the review queue channel every two hours. Escalate to Maren Strand if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Playbook: undoing a tuning change
content: Use this playbook when a tuning change closes cases it should not. Step 1: Turn the tuning change off in the rules console. Step 2: Replay the previous month's alerts without it. Step 3: Reopen any case the change closed while it was live. Escalate to Omar Sato if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Tuning board summary: name matching
content: Attendees: Pavel Abara, Nadia Toivonen and Omar Sato. Update: the tuning board will meet every second Wednesday. Risk raised: a looser name match could miss a true hit, so every change is replayed first. Decided: every tuning change is replayed on past alerts before it goes live. Follow-up: KYC-16 sets up a tuning board that meets every second Wednesday.

title: Tuning board summary: thresholds
content: Attendees: Arjun Weber, Omar Sato and Pavel Abara. Discussed: a replay showed scores change for less than 10% of cases. Score thresholds are set by the risk committee. Next step: KYC-18 reviews score thresholds with the risk committee.

title: How to escalate a case
content: This guide explains how to escalate a case to a senior analyst. First, check the case score and the failed checks. Then assign the case to the senior analyst on shift. Finally, add a second reviewer before you close the case. Ask in #kyc-automation if something fails.

title: Analyst training guide
content: This page covers what a new analyst learns in the first two weeks. The training guide covers the 12 most common case types. Each new analyst reviews 10 sample cases before going live. The first training week covers the review queue and the case types.

title: Audit evidence index
content: This page explains where the evidence for each closed case is kept. Every closed case keeps its evidence for seven years. Evidence records cannot be edited once a case closes. The last audit sample found two cases with a missing screenshot.

title: Audit sampling method
content: Background: the evidence index lists 18 thousand closed cases. Decision: auditors sample 50 closed cases every three months. Each evidence record links the case, the analyst and the rule version. Maren Strand approved this after the review.

title: Audit findings log
content: Attendees: Omar Sato, Nadia Toivonen and Arjun Weber. Discussed: the last audit sample found two cases with a missing screenshot. Decided: auditors sample 50 closed cases every three months. Follow-up: KYC-10 builds an index of evidence by case, analyst and rule version.

title: Corporate card rewards master page
content: Goal: corporate cardholders earn rewards on every purchase, with clear tiers and no surprise caps. Status: the reward tiers are signed off and the pricing sheet is final. The partner terms are with legal for a last review. Go-live follows the signed partner terms and a four-week pilot. Key issues: CARD-2, CARD-3, CARD-5 and CARD-7. CARD-3 is blocked because it waits on legal's review of the termination clause. Plan of record: the Partner terms summary in Drive. Decided: points never expire while the account is open. Owner: Kenji Petrov.

title: Reward tier design
content: This page describes the three reward tiers and how cardholders move between them. Standard earns 1 point per dollar and Premier earns 2. Tier upgrades happen at the start of each billing cycle. A cardholder moves up a tier after spending 50 thousand dollars in a year. Designed by Arjun Weber and reviewed by Gustav Eriksen. Open question: Do points expire when a cardholder leaves their company?

title: Decision record: points never expire
content: Background: Plus earns 1.5 points per dollar. Decision: points never expire while the account is open. There are three reward tiers called Standard, Plus and Premier. Approved by Andre Hoffmann at the team sync.

title: Decision record: yearly cashback cap
content: Background: travel spend earns double points up to the cap. Decision: cashback is capped at 2,000 dollars a year per card. Cardholders see their cap progress on the rewards page. Gustav Eriksen approved this after the review.

title: Rewards sync: pricing sign-off
content: Attendees: Nadia Toivonen, Keiko Duarte and Andre Hoffmann. Update: finance signed off the pricing model. The pricing sheet models 4,800 cardholders in the first year. Action: CARD-13 tracks reward cost as a share of spend each week.

title: Rewards sync: partner terms
content: Attendees: Wren Ortiz, Andre Hoffmann and Kenji Petrov. Update: the issuer funds the points earned on travel spend. Risk raised: go-live could slip if the termination clause needs another round. Legal is reviewing the termination clause. Next step: CARD-10 sets up the daily spend data feed from the partner.

title: How to add a reward category
content: This guide explains how to add a new reward category. First, find the merchant codes for the new category in the issuer's list. Then add the category and its earn rate to the mapping sheet. Finally, test a purchase in the sandbox before the change goes live. Ask in #card-rewards if something fails.

title: Rewards page design
content: This page describes what cardholders see on the rewards page. The rewards page shows points, tier and cap progress. The tier badge uses the brand colours. The rewards page works on phones as well as on desktop browsers. Designed by Arjun Weber and reviewed by Wren Ortiz.

title: Corporate rewards pilot plan
content: This page describes the four-week pilot before go-live. Go-live follows the signed partner terms. Pilot cardholders get a short survey after two weeks. The pilot ends with a review of points, caps and support questions. Designed by Gustav Eriksen and reviewed by Wren Ortiz.

title: Spend category rules
content: This page covers the spend categories and their earn rates. Spend is grouped into 9 categories for rewards. Category rules follow the issuer's merchant codes. The category list is reviewed with finance every six months.

title: Partner API integration master page
content: Goal: the partner's systems create and track orders through our public API, with webhooks they can rely on. Status: the API contract is signed and the sandbox is open to the partner. Webhook retries pass in the sandbox. Production go-live waits on the rate limit test. Key issues: VEND-1, VEND-2, VEND-3 and VEND-4. VEND-3 is blocked because it waits on the partner's test window. Plan of record: the Signed partner API contract in Drive. Decided: version 1 of the contract is frozen for six months. Owner: Ruben Schmidt.

title: Partner API contract
content: This page covers the endpoints, fields and error codes of version 1. The API contract covers orders, shipments and webhooks. Version 1 of the contract is frozen for six months. Wei Ming signed off the field names for the partner team.

title: Sandbox setup guide
content: This guide explains how to make a first call against the sandbox. The sandbox was shared with Wei Ming and the two partner contractors. First, ask for a test key in the partner channel. Then call the orders endpoint with the test key and check the response. Finally, send a test webhook from the sandbox console and acknowledge it. Ask in #vend-sandbox if something fails.

title: Webhook retry design
content: This design explains how failed webhooks are retried and deduplicated. Each webhook will carry an idempotency key. The partner acknowledges a webhook within 5 seconds. A repeated webhook is processed only once. Designed by Dmitri Ueda and reviewed by Kwame Varga. Open question: What happens if the partner is down for a whole day?

title: Partner commercial review
content: Attendees: Ruben Schmidt, Ada Pereira and Kwame Varga. Update: the rate limit test runs against the sandbox before go-live. Risk raised: go-live could slip if the partner's test window moves again. The partner may send 50 requests per second.

title: Engineering handbook
content: This page explains how engineering teams work day to day. Core hours run from 10:00 to 16:00 in each office. Design reviews happen before work starts on anything that takes more than two weeks. Engineers keep one day a month for learning.

title: Working agreements
content: This page explains the agreements every engineering team keeps. Every repository has a code owners file. Design reviews happen before work starts on anything that takes more than two weeks. Engineers keep one day a month for learning.

title: On-call guide
content: This guide explains how to handle a page during your on-call week. First, acknowledge the page within 15 minutes. Then post what you see in the team channel. Finally, call the team lead if the problem lasts more than an hour. Ask in #eng-on-call if something fails.

title: On-call rota rules
content: This page covers how on-call rotas are planned and swapped. Each team runs a weekly on-call rota from Monday to Monday. The on-call engineer answers a page within 15 minutes. A page that lasts more than an hour goes to the team lead.

title: Paging and escalation guide
content: Use this playbook when a page is not resolved within an hour. Step 1: Acknowledge the page within 15 minutes. Step 2: Post what you see in the team channel. Step 3: Call the team lead if the problem lasts more than an hour. Escalate to Dmitri Ueda if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Code review guide
content: This guide explains how to review a pull request. First, read the description and the linked ticket first. Then run the change locally if it touches more than one service. Finally, approve, or ask for changes with a clear reason. Ask in #eng-code-review if something fails.

title: Pull request size guide
content: This page explains how big a pull request may be. Every pull request needs one approval from a code owner. Reviewers answer within one working day. Comments marked nit never block a merge.

title: Architecture principles
content: This page covers the principles every service follows. Services talk to each other through versioned APIs. Each service lists its owner and on-call rota in the service catalogue. A service reads another service's data only through its API.

title: Service ownership map
content: This page covers which team owns each service. A new service needs an architecture review before its first deploy. Shared libraries have a named maintainer. A replaced API stays available for one release after the new one ships.

title: Deploy policy
content: This policy covers when and how code is deployed. Deploys run from 09:00 to 16:00 on working days. Every deploy can be rolled back within 10 minutes. Exceptions to the freeze need approval from two leads. Questions go to Dmitri Ueda.

title: Deploy freeze rules
content: This policy covers deploy freezes before public holidays. Deploys run from 09:00 to 16:00 on working days. A deploy freeze starts two days before a public holiday. Every deploy can be rolled back within 10 minutes. Questions go to Clara Rahman.

title: Search service playbook: slow queries
content: Use this playbook when search latency stays above 800 milliseconds. Step 1: Find the slowest queries in the search dashboard. Step 2: Check whether the index rebuild is still running. Step 3: Move traffic to the standby index if latency stays above 800 milliseconds. Call Priya Silva if it is not fixed within an hour.

title: Search service playbook: index rebuild
content: Use this playbook when the nightly index rebuild runs late. Step 1: Find the slowest queries in the search dashboard. Step 2: Check whether the index rebuild is still running. Step 3: Move traffic to the standby index if latency stays above 800 milliseconds. Call Clara Rahman if it is not fixed within an hour.

title: Search service overview
content: This design explains how the search service indexes and answers queries. The search index is rebuilt every night at 03:00. Slow queries above 800 milliseconds are logged with their plan. A full index rebuild takes 95 minutes. Designed by Priya Silva and reviewed by Bastian Lopez. Open question: Why did search slow down after 03:00 last night?

title: Notification service playbook: delayed messages
content: Use this playbook when messages wait in the queue for more than five minutes. Step 1: Check the queue depth on the notification dashboard. Step 2: Scale the senders if the queue grows for more than ten minutes. Step 3: Tell support if messages are more than an hour late. Call Clara Rahman if it is not fixed within an hour.

title: Notification service playbook: bounced emails
content: Use this playbook when bounced emails rise above the usual level. Step 1: Check the queue depth on the notification dashboard. Step 2: Scale the senders if the queue grows for more than ten minutes. Step 3: Tell support if messages are more than an hour late. Escalate to Ruben Schmidt if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Notification service overview
content: This page describes how the notification service queues and sends messages. The notification service sends 2.3 million messages a day. Push messages leave the queue within 30 seconds. Bounced emails are retried once and then dropped. Dmitri Ueda owns this design, and Clara Rahman reviewed it. Open question: Can marketing send a big campaign on Monday morning?

title: Identity service playbook: login errors
content: Use this playbook when login errors rise above 2% of attempts. Step 1: Check the login error rate by app on the identity dashboard. Step 2: Look for a recent deploy of the identity service. Step 3: Roll back the deploy if errors started with it. Call Ayla Rossi if it is not fixed within an hour.

title: Identity service playbook: signing key rotation
content: Use this playbook when the token signing key is due for rotation. Step 1: Check the login error rate by app on the identity dashboard. Step 2: Look for a recent deploy of the identity service. Step 3: Roll back the deploy if errors started with it. Escalate to Ayla Rossi if the problem lasts more than an hour.

title: Identity service overview

title: Leave policy
content: This policy covers annual leave and how to book it. Everyone gets 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays. Up to five unused days carry over to the next year. Leave is booked in the HR system at least two weeks ahead for anything longer than a week. Questions go to Viktor Keller.

title: Remote work policy

title: Learning budget policy

title: Code of conduct

title: Equipment policy

title: CARD-5 Run a four-week pilot
content: CARD-5 runs a four-week pilot with the first 200 cardholders. Background: support agents get a rewards guide before the pilot starts. Acceptance: pilot cardholders earn and see points without errors.

title: CARD-6 Map merchant codes to categories
content: CARD-6 maps the issuer's merchant codes to 9 reward categories. Background: a merchant code that fits no category earns the standard rate. Acceptance: every test purchase lands in the right category.

title: CARD-7 Build the rewards page
content: CARD-7 builds the rewards page with points, tier and cap progress. Background: the cap progress bar turns amber at 80% of the cap. Acceptance: the page matches the approved design.

title: CARD-8 Upgrade tiers at the start of each cycle
content: CARD-8 upgrades a cardholder's tier at the start of each billing cycle. For context, Standard earns 1 point per dollar and Premier earns 2. Acceptance: a test upgrade applies on the first day of the cycle.

title: CARD-9 Write the support rewards guide
content: CARD-9 writes the rewards guide for support agents. Context: the first 200 cardholders join a pilot for four weeks. Acceptance: agents answer the 10 most common questions from the guide.

title: DATA-1 Partition the event staging table by hour
content: DATA-1 partitions the event staging table by hour so loads can run every 15 minutes. For context, each ingestion job writes to a staging table before the main table. Agreed: Leon Torres partitions the event staging table by hour. Acceptance: the event stream job loads every 15 minutes for a week.

title: DATA-10 Limit backfills to night hours
content: DATA-10 limits backfills to the hours between 22:00 and 06:00. For context, the two-year backfill of events finished in six nights. Acceptance: no backfill runs during working hours for four weeks.

title: DATA-11 Require approval for large queries
content: DATA-11 requires approval for queries that scan more than 50 GB. For context, each team sees its query costs in a weekly summary. Acceptance: large queries show an approval prompt.

title: DATA-12 Show query cost per dashboard
content: DATA-12 shows the scan size of each dashboard query. Background: a query that scans more than 50 GB needs approval. Acceptance: every dashboard shows its average scan size.

title: DATA-13 Add a data owner review to schema changes
content: DATA-13 adds a required data owner review to schema change pull requests. For context, a breaking change is announced two weeks before it applies. Acceptance: no schema change merges without an owner review.

title: DATA-14 Announce breaking schema changes
content: DATA-14 posts breaking schema changes two weeks before they apply. Background: schema changes go through a pull request with a data owner review. Acceptance: every breaking change has an announcement two weeks ahead.

title: DATA-15 Alert table owners on stale data
content: DATA-15 alerts the table owner when the newest row is older than three hours. For context, the two-hour target applies to the 30 main tables. Acceptance: a test alert reaches the owner.

title: DATA-16 Measure freshness for the main tables
content: DATA-16 measures the age of the newest row in each of the 30 main tables. Context: a freshness alert goes to the table owner after three hours. Acceptance: the freshness view covers all 30 main tables.

title: DATA-17 Move the support tickets job
content: DATA-17 moves the support tickets job to the new warehouse. Background: a failed load is retried three times before it pages the data on-call engineer. Acceptance: ticket data reaches the warehouse within two hours.

title: DATA-18 Retry failed loads three times
content: DATA-18 retries a failed load three times before paging the data on-call engineer. For context, each ingestion job writes to a staging table before the main table. Acceptance: fewer than two loads a week page the on-call engineer.

title: DATA-19 Move the activation dashboard
content: DATA-19 moves the activation dashboard to the new warehouse. For context, the revenue dashboard waits on a finance sign-off. Acceptance: the product team signs off the activation numbers.

title: DATA-2 Move the billing events job
content: DATA-2 moves the billing events job to the new warehouse. It waits on read access to the billing source. Acceptance: billing events reach the warehouse within two hours.

title: DATA-20 Describe every customer table column
content: DATA-20 adds a description and an owner to every column of the customer table. Background: 26 of 30 main tables meet the two-hour freshness target. Acceptance: each of the 42 columns has a description and an owner.

title: DATA-21 Score churn on the new tables
content: DATA-21 moves the churn model inputs to the new customer and activity tables. Context: the churn model scores every account each night. Acceptance: nightly scores match the old model within 1%.

title: DATA-22 Review churn model features with risk
content: DATA-22 reviews the churn model features with the risk analysts. It waits for the risk team's monthly review slot. Acceptance: the risk team signs off the feature list.

title: DATA-23 Drop tables nobody queries
content: DATA-23 drops tables that nobody queried in 90 days. Context: the five most expensive queries make up half of the monthly bill. Acceptance: storage falls by at least 15%.

title: DATA-24 Add null checks to the event tables
content: DATA-24 adds null checks to the 12 event tables. For context, most failed checks trace back to a late export from a source system. Acceptance: a broken load fails its null check in a test.

title: DATA-25 Add freshness to the team dashboard
content: DATA-25 adds the freshness view to the data team dashboard. For context, the billing events table is the stalest, at about 9 hours. Acceptance: the team dashboard shows freshness for every main table.

title: DATA-26 Retire the old analytics cluster
content: DATA-26 shuts down the old analytics cluster after the last dashboard moves. For context, the revenue dashboard waits on a finance sign-off. Acceptance: no dashboard reads from the old cluster for two weeks.

title: DATA-27 Backfill the support tickets history
content: DATA-27 backfills three years of support tickets. Background: backfills run only between 22:00 and 06:00. Risk: a long backfill could overlap working hours and slow the dashboards. Acceptance: ticket counts match the source for every week.

title: DATA-28 Write the column naming guide
content: DATA-28 writes the naming guide for warehouse columns. Context: renamed columns keep an alias for two weeks. Background: new columns are added at the end of a table. Acceptance: new tables follow the guide at their first review.

title: DATA-3 Stop dashboards when a check fails
content: DATA-3 stops dashboard refreshes when a quality check fails. Background: 128 quality checks run after every load. For context, a warning check posts in the quality channel without stopping anything. Acceptance: a failed check holds every linked dashboard.

title: DATA-4 Compare row counts with each source
content: DATA-4 compares nightly row counts with each source system. For context, each quality check has an owner and a severity. Acceptance: a mismatch above 0.5% opens a ticket.

title: DATA-5 Move the churn dashboard
content: DATA-5 moves the churn dashboard to the new warehouse. Background: dashboard owners sign off before an old version is removed. Acceptance: the churn dashboard refreshes every hour from the new warehouse.

title: DATA-6 Move the revenue dashboard
content: DATA-6 moves the revenue dashboard to the new warehouse. Context: dashboard owners sign off before an old version is removed. Acceptance: finance signs off the new revenue numbers.

title: DATA-7 Partition the customer table by day
content: DATA-7 partitions the customer table by day and clusters it by account. For context, new column names follow the naming guide. Acceptance: account lookups scan less than 1 GB.

title: DATA-8 Apply the naming guide to old columns
content: DATA-8 renames 64 old columns to follow the naming guide. Context: the customer table holds one row per account with 42 columns. Acceptance: every column in the main tables follows the naming guide.

title: DATA-9 Backfill two years of events
content: DATA-9 backfills two years of events into the new warehouse. Background: a backfill writes to a copy of the table and swaps it in at the end. Acceptance: row counts match the source for every day.

title: KYC-1 Clear simple cases automatically
content: KYC-1 clears cases where every automatic check passes. For context, every automatic decision is logged with the inputs it used. Acceptance: at least 55% of cases close without an analyst for two weeks.

title: KYC-10 Build the audit evidence index
content: KYC-10 builds an index of evidence by case, analyst and rule version. For context, every closed case keeps its evidence for seven years. Acceptance: the index finds any case in under 10 seconds.

title: KYC-11 Read document expiry dates
content: KYC-11 reads the expiry date and issuing country from identity documents. Context: a document photo that is too dark fails the document check. Acceptance: expired documents are never cleared automatically.

title: KYC-12 Add account age to the risk score
content: KYC-12 adds account age to the risk score. Context: the risk score combines country, product and account age. Acceptance: scores change for less than 10% of cases in a replay.

title: KYC-13 Write the analyst training guide
content: KYC-13 writes the training guide for the 12 most common case types. Context: in the second week each new analyst works live cases with a senior analyst. Acceptance: two new analysts finish training with it.

title: KYC-14 Measure handling time per case type
content: KYC-14 measures handling time for each case type. Background: complex cases still take over an hour. For context, pre-filled case summaries save about 9 minutes per case. Acceptance: the dashboard shows handling time by case type.

title: KYC-15 Log every automatic decision
content: KYC-15 logs every automatic decision with the inputs it used. For context, automatic checks clear 58% of cases without an analyst. Acceptance: an auditor can rebuild any decision from the log.

title: KYC-16 Hold a tuning board every second Wednesday
content: KYC-16 sets up a tuning board that meets every second Wednesday. For context, name matching ignores accents and word order. Acceptance: each tuning change has a board decision.

title: KYC-17 Staff the queue from 08:00 to 20:00
content: KYC-17 sets queue staffing from 08:00 to 20:00 on weekdays. For context, cases older than one working day are flagged in red. Acceptance: no case waits more than an hour during staffed hours.

title: KYC-18 Review score thresholds with the risk committee
content: KYC-18 reviews score thresholds with the risk committee. It waits on the risk committee's next meeting. Background: the risk score combines country, product and account age. Acceptance: the committee signs off the thresholds.

title: KYC-19 Add sample cases to training
content: KYC-19 adds 10 sample cases for each new analyst. For context, trainees pass a short quiz before they work alone. Acceptance: every new analyst reviews 10 samples before going live.

title: KYC-2 Replay tuning changes on past alerts
content: KYC-2 replays each tuning change on the previous month's alerts before it goes live. Background: false positives fell from 71% to 44% of alerts. Agreed: Maren Strand replays each tuning change on the previous month's alerts. Acceptance: every tuning change shows its replay result.

title: KYC-20 Track escalation rates
content: KYC-20 tracks the share of cases that escalate each week. Context: an escalated case needs a second reviewer before it closes. Acceptance: the weekly view shows escalation rates by team.

title: KYC-21 Send failed checks to an analyst
content: KYC-21 sends any case with a failed check to an analyst. For context, automatic checks run within two minutes of a case arriving. Acceptance: no case with a failed check closes automatically.

title: KYC-22 Plan weekend cover
content: KYC-22 plans weekend cover with one analyst on call. It waits on approval for weekend allowances. Background: the review queue holds 340 cases, down from 1,200. Acceptance: the backlog stays under 400 cases on Monday mornings.

title: KYC-3 Ignore accents in name matching
content: KYC-3 makes name matching ignore accents and word order. For context, each tuning change is replayed on the previous month's alerts before it goes live. Acceptance: false positives drop below 50% of alerts.

title: KYC-4 Order the queue by risk score
content: KYC-4 orders the review queue by risk score instead of arrival time. For context, the review queue holds 340 cases, down from 1,200. Acceptance: the highest scoring case is always at the top.

title: KYC-5 Flag cases older than one working day
content: KYC-5 flags cases older than one working day in red. Background: analysts pick cases in order of risk score. Acceptance: the queue view shows every overdue case in red.

title: KYC-6 Pre-fill case summaries
content: KYC-6 pre-fills each case summary from the automatic checks. Background: the median handling time is 14 minutes, down from 31. Acceptance: median handling time drops below 15 minutes.

title: KYC-7 Route high scores to senior analysts
content: KYC-7 routes cases scoring above 80 to a senior analyst. Context: escalations dropped by 20% after the scoring change. Acceptance: no case above 80 is closed by a junior analyst.

title: KYC-8 Require a second reviewer for escalations
content: KYC-8 requires a second reviewer before an escalated case closes. Context: cases scoring above 80 go to a senior analyst. Context: escalations dropped by 20% after the scoring change. Acceptance: every escalated case shows two reviewers.

title: KYC-9 Keep evidence with each closed case
content: KYC-9 keeps the evidence of each closed case for seven years. For context, auditors sample 50 closed cases every three months. Acceptance: auditors find the evidence for any sampled case.

title: MOB-1 Stage the Android rollout
content: MOB-1 moves the Android rollout through 25%, 50% and 100% of users. For context, the rollout pauses on its own if crashes double within an hour. Acceptance: each step holds for 48 hours with a crash-free rate of at least 99.5%.

title: MOB-10 Shrink the font files
content: MOB-10 replaces the full font files with subsets for the supported languages. Background: scrolling stays at 60 frames per second on mid-range phones. Acceptance: the app grows by less than 2 MB in 4.0.

title: MOB-11 Triage beta feedback every Monday
content: MOB-11 sets a Monday triage for beta feedback with an owner per area. For context, the beta needs 300 testers with phones older than four years. Acceptance: every feedback item has an owner within a week.

title: MOB-12 Alert the team on crash spikes
content: MOB-12 alerts the team channel when crashes double within an hour. Context: crash alerts reach the team channel within 5 minutes. Acceptance: a test spike reaches the channel within 5 minutes.

title: MOB-13 Start the iOS rollout at 5%
content: MOB-13 starts the iOS rollout at 5% once store review passes. Context: each rollout step waits 48 hours and needs a crash-free rate of 99.5%. Acceptance: the iOS rollout reaches 5% with a crash-free rate of 99.5%.

title: MOB-14 Put offline mode behind a flag
content: MOB-14 puts offline mode behind a flag for 20% of beta testers. Context: sync conflicts resolve in favour of the most recent edit. Acceptance: the flag can be turned off for everyone within 10 minutes.

title: MOB-15 Refresh the store screenshots
content: MOB-15 refreshes the store screenshots for the new home screen. Context: the iOS build has been in store review for two days. Acceptance: both stores show the new screenshots.

title: MOB-16 Update the location privacy label
content: MOB-16 updates the privacy label for the new location prompt. For context, store screenshots were refreshed for the new home screen. Acceptance: both stores show the approved label text.

title: MOB-17 Adjust dark theme colours
content: MOB-17 adjusts dark theme colours to meet the contrast guideline. Context: the new home screen puts the three most used actions at the top. Acceptance: every text colour reaches a contrast ratio of 4.5 to 1.

title: MOB-18 Freeze the branch for the release candidate
content: MOB-18 freezes the 4.0 branch on Tuesday before the candidate build. For context, the 4.0 branch was cut after the beta sign-off. Acceptance: only crash fixes merge after the freeze.

title: MOB-19 Recruit beta testers with older phones
content: MOB-19 recruits 300 beta testers with phones older than four years. Background: the beta sign-off needs two weeks without a new top crash. Acceptance: the beta has at least 300 testers on older phones.

title: MOB-2 Fix the image caching crash on older phones
content: MOB-2 fixes the image caching crash on Android phones with less than 3 GB of memory. Context: the crash-free rate on the beta is 99.6%. Agreed: Ingrid Tanaka ships the image caching fix in the next train. Acceptance: no image caching crash appears on the beta for a week.

title: MOB-20 Keep scrolling at 60 frames per second
content: MOB-20 removes layout work from the activity list. For context, cold start time dropped from 2.8 to 1.9 seconds. Acceptance: scrolling stays at 60 frames per second on mid-range phones.

title: MOB-21 Keep 30 days of activity offline
content: MOB-21 keeps the last 30 days of activity on the phone. Background: the next build shows when the app last synced and what is waiting to upload. Acceptance: the activity screen opens offline with 30 days of data.

title: MOB-22 Fix the last two accessibility findings
content: MOB-22 fixes the last two findings from the accessibility audit. Background: the two open audit findings are on the settings screens. Acceptance: the audit shows no open finding.

title: MOB-23 Add device context to crash alerts
content: MOB-23 adds the phone model and memory to every crash alert. For context, a release stops if the crash-free rate drops below 99%. Acceptance: every crash alert names the phone model.

title: MOB-24 Write the 4.0 release checklist
content: MOB-24 writes the checklist each release captain follows. For context, the release candidate carries 212 merged pull requests. For context, the 4.0 branch was cut after the beta sign-off. Acceptance: two release captains use it without questions.

title: MOB-25 Add a rollout pause control
content: MOB-25 adds a control that pauses the staged rollout at its current step. It waits on store console permissions for the release captains. Acceptance: a test pause holds the rollout for 24 hours.

title: MOB-26 Test the new home screen with customers
content: MOB-26 runs usability tests of the new home screen with 12 customers. Background: the new home screen puts the three most used actions at the top. Acceptance: at least 9 of 12 customers finish the top three tasks faster.

title: MOB-27 Close the 4.0 beta
content: MOB-27 closes the 4.0 beta once the rollout passes 50%. Context: beta feedback is triaged every Monday. Acceptance: beta testers move to the public build without a reinstall.

title: MOB-28 Write the 4.0 store text
content: MOB-28 writes the store release text for 4.0 in five languages. Background: the location privacy label changes in 4.0. Acceptance: both stores show the text in every supported language.

title: MOB-29 Show sync status in the app
content: MOB-29 shows when the app last synced and what is waiting to upload. Context: offline mode keeps the last 30 days of activity on the phone. Acceptance: testers can see waiting changes on every screen.

title: MOB-3 Answer the iOS store review questions
content: MOB-3 answers the store review questions about the account deletion flow. It waits on the store review team to reply. Context: store screenshots were refreshed for the new home screen. Acceptance: the iOS build passes store review.

title: MOB-30 Measure startup on older phones
content: MOB-30 adds startup timing for phones older than four years. Background: scrolling stays at 60 frames per second on mid-range phones. Acceptance: the dashboard shows startup time by phone age.

title: MOB-31 Fix the camera permission crash
content: MOB-31 fixes a crash when the camera permission is revoked during a scan. Context: crash alerts will name the phone model and its memory. Acceptance: no camera permission crash appears on the beta for a week.

title: MOB-32 Plan the 4.1 train
content: MOB-32 plans the scope of the 4.1 train after the rollout. Background: hotfixes go out between trains only when the crash-free rate drops below 99%. Acceptance: the 4.1 scope is agreed by the product and mobile leads.

title: MOB-4 Cut the 4.0 release branch
content: MOB-4 cuts the 4.0 branch after the beta sign-off. Context: a new build leaves the release train every second Thursday. Acceptance: the branch builds green on both platforms.

title: MOB-5 Resolve offline sync conflicts
content: MOB-5 resolves sync conflicts in favour of the most recent edit. For context, offline edits wait in a queue and upload in the order they were made. Acceptance: no edit is lost in a test with 500 offline changes.

title: MOB-6 Build the new home screen
content: MOB-6 builds the new home screen with the three most used actions at the top. For context, the new home screen ships on both platforms in 4.0. Acceptance: the home screen matches the approved design on both platforms.

title: MOB-7 Add screen reader labels to the home screen
content: MOB-7 adds a screen reader label to every button on the home screen. Background: text scales up to 200% without clipping. Acceptance: the accessibility audit finds no unlabelled button.

title: MOB-8 Fix text clipping at large font sizes
content: MOB-8 fixes text that clips when the font scale goes above 150%. Background: the accessibility audit found 9 problems and 7 are fixed. Acceptance: text scales to 200% without clipping on every screen.

title: MOB-9 Cut cold start time
content: MOB-9 removes three startup tasks that block the first screen. Background: the app grew by 4 MB because of the new fonts. Acceptance: cold start stays under 2 seconds on mid-range phones.

title: PLAT-1 Add runners to the second rack
content: PLAT-1 adds 24 runners to the second rack for the last 18 build jobs. It waits on finance approval for the host order. Acceptance: all 80 jobs run on the new pool for a full week, and the old pool is drained.

title: PLAT-10 Expire old build artifacts
content: PLAT-10 deletes build artifacts older than 30 days from the artifact store. For context, release artifacts are kept for a year. Acceptance: the store stays under 4 TB for four weeks in a row.

title: PLAT-11 Retry steps that fail on network timeouts
content: PLAT-11 retries a build step once when it fails on a network timeout. For context, runner registration tokens rotate every 30 days. Acceptance: timeout failures drop below 1% of builds.

title: PLAT-12 Move the docs site build
content: PLAT-12 moves the documentation site build to the new pool. Context: jobs move in groups of ten, and each group runs a full night before the next one moves. Acceptance: the docs site publishes from the new pool for two weeks.

title: PLAT-13 Show runner minutes per team
content: PLAT-13 adds a monthly runner minutes budget per team with an alert at 80%. For context, each team sees its share of runner minutes on the dashboard every Monday. Acceptance: each team sees its usage on the dashboard every Monday.

title: PLAT-14 Remove the old runner autoscaler
content: PLAT-14 removes the autoscaler that served the old pool. It waits until the old pool is drained. For context, the host order for the second rack waits on finance approval. Acceptance: no job references the old autoscaler for a week.

title: PLAT-15 Cache Gradle dependencies on the runner image
content: PLAT-15 bakes common Gradle dependencies into the runner image. Context: each new runner image goes to one canary host before the rest. Acceptance: Android builds download less than 200 MB per run.

title: PLAT-16 Split slow integration tests
content: PLAT-16 moves the 40 slowest integration tests into their own nightly job. For context, no shard runs longer than 6 minutes on the new pool. Acceptance: the pull request pipeline drops under 12 minutes at the median.

title: PLAT-17 Alert on runner queue time
content: PLAT-17 alerts the on-call engineer when jobs wait more than 5 minutes for a runner. Context: the slowest stage of each job is highlighted in the duration view. Acceptance: the alert fires in a test and pages the right rota.

title: PLAT-18 Document the runner pool layout
content: PLAT-18 writes up how the two racks, labels and pools fit together. For context, the old pool runs on 70 hosts that are three years past their support date. Acceptance: a new engineer finds the right label for a job in one read.

title: PLAT-19 Rotate runner registration tokens
content: PLAT-19 rotates the runner registration tokens every 30 days. Context: release tags are created by the pipeline instead of by hand. Acceptance: no runner uses a token older than 30 days.

title: PLAT-2 Warm the shared cache before nightly builds
content: PLAT-2 starts the cache warm-up 40 minutes before the nightly builds. Background: the shared cache serves 81% of build steps, up from 64% before the upgrade. Acceptance: the first nightly build reads at least 80% of its steps from the cache.

title: PLAT-20 Fix the cache key for monorepo builds
content: PLAT-20 adds the lockfile hash to the cache key. Context: cache keys include the lockfile hash, so a dependency bump starts a fresh entry. Acceptance: cache hits stay above 75% after a dependency bump.

title: PLAT-21 Move the frontend lint jobs
content: PLAT-21 moves the 12 frontend lint jobs to the new pool. For context, 62 of 80 build jobs run on the new pool and 18 still use the old one. Acceptance: lint jobs finish in under 3 minutes on the new pool.

title: PLAT-22 Build a flaky test dashboard
content: PLAT-22 lists flaky tests by failure count and owner. Background: a test moves to quarantine after three failures in a row on the main branch. Acceptance: the weekly review uses the dashboard instead of a spreadsheet.

title: PLAT-23 Drain the old pool on weekends
content: PLAT-23 drains the old pool on weekends to save hosts. Background: the 18 remaining jobs are the iOS and Android packaging jobs. Acceptance: the old pool runs no weekend jobs for two weeks.

title: PLAT-24 Run smoke tests on every merge
content: PLAT-24 runs a 4-minute smoke suite after each merge to the main branch. For context, the average wait in the merge queue is 9 minutes. Acceptance: a failed smoke run stops the next deploy.

title: PLAT-25 Add disk cleanup to runners
content: PLAT-25 cleans the runner disk when it passes 85% full. For context, common Gradle dependencies are baked into the runner image. Acceptance: no build fails on a full disk for four weeks.

title: PLAT-26 Measure build time per stage
content: PLAT-26 records the duration of every build stage. For context, queue time alerts page the platform on-call engineer after 5 minutes. Acceptance: the dashboard shows the slowest stage of each job.

title: PLAT-27 Move release tagging into the pipeline
content: PLAT-27 creates release tags from the pipeline instead of by hand. Context: 37 pipeline variables are no longer read by any job. Acceptance: three releases in a row are tagged by the pipeline.

title: PLAT-28 Limit parallel jobs per branch
content: PLAT-28 limits each branch to 4 parallel jobs. Background: the merge queue will test up to 6 pull requests in one batch. Acceptance: queue time stays under 5 minutes during the morning peak.

title: PLAT-29 Archive the old build scripts
content: PLAT-29 moves the old shell build scripts into an archive folder. Context: release tags are created by the pipeline instead of by hand. Acceptance: no active job calls an archived script.

title: PLAT-3 Quarantine a test after three failures
content: PLAT-3 moves a test to quarantine after three failures in a row on the main branch. For context, the weekly flaky review lists 14 quarantined tests. Acceptance: every quarantined test has an owner within one working day.

title: PLAT-30 Share the cache with fork builds
content: PLAT-30 lets fork builds read the shared cache without writing to it. Background: only builds on the main branch write to the shared cache. Acceptance: fork builds reach a 60% cache hit rate.

title: PLAT-31 Upgrade the runner agent
content: PLAT-31 upgrades the runner agent on all 56 hosts. It waits for the agent maintainers to publish a fixed build. Acceptance: every host reports the new agent version.

title: PLAT-32 Track the cost per build
content: PLAT-32 estimates the host cost of each build from its runner minutes. Background: the new pool costs 22% less per build than the old pool. Acceptance: the monthly cost view matches the finance export within 5%.

title: PLAT-33 Retire the nightly full rebuild
content: PLAT-33 replaces the nightly full rebuild with cached incremental builds. For context, the cache warm-up takes 11 minutes and runs before the nightly builds. Acceptance: nightly builds take under 25 minutes.

title: PLAT-34 Test each runner image on a canary host
content: PLAT-34 rolls each new runner image to one canary host first. Background: a runner disk that passes 85% full slows every job on that host. Acceptance: a broken image never reaches more than one host.

title: PLAT-35 Write the pipeline style guide
content: PLAT-35 sets naming and layout rules for pipeline files. Context: the old shell build scripts are moving into an archive folder. Acceptance: new pipelines pass the lint check on the first try.

title: PLAT-36 Clean up unused pipeline variables
content: PLAT-36 removes 37 pipeline variables that no job reads. Context: the old shell build scripts are moving into an archive folder. Acceptance: the variable list keeps only the ones in use.

title: PLAT-4 Move the Android packaging jobs
content: PLAT-4 moves the 9 Android packaging jobs to the new runner pool. Context: the host order for the second rack waits on finance approval. Acceptance: Android release builds pass three nights in a row on the new pool.

title: PLAT-5 Move the iOS packaging jobs
content: PLAT-5 moves the 9 iOS packaging jobs once the second rack is ready. For context, a job move is reversed if its median build time grows by more than 10%. Agreed: Lina Engel moves the iOS jobs after the capacity fix. Acceptance: iOS release builds pass three nights in a row on the new pool.

title: PLAT-6 Batch pull requests in the merge queue
content: PLAT-6 lets the merge queue test up to 6 pull requests in one batch. For context, a failed batch is split in half until the failing pull request is found. Acceptance: the average wait in the queue stays under 10 minutes for two weeks.

title: PLAT-7 Shard the backend test suite
content: PLAT-7 splits the backend test suite into 8 shards by recorded duration. Context: the pull request pipeline takes 11 minutes at the median. Acceptance: no shard runs longer than 6 minutes on the new pool.

title: PLAT-8 Pin the base image for build containers
content: PLAT-8 pins the build container base image and rebuilds it every Monday. For context, Android builds now download less than 200 MB per run. Acceptance: two builds a week apart produce the same image digest.

title: PLAT-9 Show the cache hit rate per job
content: PLAT-9 adds the cache hit rate of each job to the build dashboard. Background: the build dashboard shows the queue time and duration of every job. Acceptance: the dashboard shows a hit rate for all 80 jobs.

title: VEND-1 Freeze version 1 of the API contract
content: VEND-1 freezes version 1 of the order and shipment API contract. Context: a breaking change needs 90 days of notice to the partner. Acceptance: the partner confirms the frozen field names.

title: VEND-2 Retry failed webhooks
content: VEND-2 retries a failed webhook 6 times over 24 hours. For context, a repeated webhook is processed only once. Acceptance: a test webhook arrives after five failed attempts.

title: VEND-3 Run the rate limit test
content: VEND-3 runs the rate limit test against the sandbox. It waits on the partner's test window. Acceptance: the sandbox holds 50 requests per second with bursts of 200.

title: VEND-4 Map partner error codes
content: VEND-4 maps the partner's error codes to our 34 stable codes. For context, every error response carries a stable code and a message. Agreed: Wei Ming owns the error code mapping for the partner. Acceptance: every partner error shows a stable code.

title: VEND-5 Rotate partner test keys
